m6-t1.introduction: A second way to understand “Design an HR dashboard for its audience”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Design for a recurring decision
sections.explanation: A dashboard should serve a known audience, action and cadence rather than accumulate every available chart.

items.label: Audience
items.detail: Name who needs the view and their authority.

items.label: Question
items.detail: Identify the recurring decision or operational concern.

items.label: Metric set
items.detail: Choose a small defined set with owners.

items.label: Action route
items.detail: Explain what to inspect or do when a signal changes.

sections.takeaway: Keep sensitive drill-down access separate from broadly shared summaries.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.
sections.section: 1. Use a small decision-led metric set

sections.title: Choose the visual form for the question
sections.explanation: Bars, lines and tables encode different relationships. The source, denominator and period must remain visible.

items.label: Category comparison
items.detail: Use labelled bars on a suitable common scale.

items.label: Time trend
items.detail: Use ordered comparable periods with missing data visible.

items.label: Exact value or action
items.detail: Use a table with units, definitions and an owner.

items.label: Disclosure check
items.detail: Ensure filtering cannot reveal a tiny or identifiable group.

sections.takeaway: Use zero-based bar lengths and labels; colour alone must not carry the meaning.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A red signal needs context and an owner
sections.explanation: Refresh time, source, definitions, filters and limitations explain what a viewer is actually seeing.

items.label: Period and refresh
items.detail: State when observations occurred and when data last updated.

items.label: Definition and source
items.detail: Link the counting rules and provenance.

items.label: Filter scope
items.detail: Show the selected population and compatible denominator.

items.label: Action and limitation
items.detail: Name the owner, next check and remaining uncertainty.

sections.takeaway: A threshold is a reviewed decision rule, not an explanation of why a result changed.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: Does a red dashboard tile explain the cause of an HR problem?
checkpoint.answer: No. It indicates a threshold under a rule. Show definitions, source, scope and limitations, then give the owner a proportionate next investigation.

m6-t2.introduction: A second way to understand “Build and quality-check a dashboard”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Separate evidence from calculations and presentation
sections.explanation: A layered workbook makes transformations and refresh behaviour inspectable. Typed chart labels can drift away from the actual data.

items.label: Raw
items.detail: Preserve the unchanged source and its provenance.

items.label: Cleaned
items.detail: Apply documented rules and log unresolved cases.

items.label: Metrics
items.detail: Calculate from the declared population and definitions.

items.label: Dashboard
items.detail: Display linked values with context and safe access.

sections.takeaway: Keep Unknown categories and definition changes visible rather than hiding incomplete records.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A filter must change both sides of a rate
sections.explanation: The synthetic acceptance fixture has whole-cohort 9/12, Source A 5/6 and Source B 4/6. Numerator and denominator must follow the same selection.

items.label: All data
items.detail: Check 9 acceptances ÷ 12 offers = 75%.

items.label: One group
items.detail: Source A uses five acceptances and six offers.

items.label: Empty selection
items.detail: Show a clear undefined state rather than a false zero rate.

items.label: Combined filters
items.detail: Reconcile both counts to the same eligible filtered records.

sections.takeaway: Source A is 5/6, not 5/12. A professional-looking chart with mismatched filters is still wrong.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A hidden tab is not an access boundary
sections.explanation: An export or viewer may expose data that the visual interface conceals. Test sharing from the intended recipient’s role.

items.label: Choose the sharing layer
items.detail: Use synthetic or safe aggregate output.

items.label: Remove restricted material
items.detail: Inspect raw tabs, identifiers and comments.

items.label: Test recipient access
items.detail: Check downloads, links and actual viewer permissions.

items.label: Review disclosure
items.detail: Consider tiny groups and complementary inference.

sections.takeaway: Publish only the necessary aggregate layer; do not rely on hiding columns or tabs to protect personal information.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: What is wrong with filtering Source A’s five acceptances while keeping all twelve offers as the denominator?
checkpoint.answer: The populations no longer match. Source A’s denominator is its six offers, so its acceptance rate is 5/6, not 5/12.

m6-t3.introduction: A second way to understand “Write an insight memo and recommend action”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Write the observation before the explanation
sections.explanation: A memo becomes reviewable when the measured result is separated from possible reasons and recommended action.

items.label: Observed result
items.detail: State the population, period, measure and comparison.

items.label: Possible explanations
items.detail: List hypotheses with their current support.

items.label: Missing evidence
items.detail: Name the check that could distinguish those explanations.

items.label: Proposed next step
items.detail: Recommend a proportionate action under an authorised owner.

sections.takeaway: Do not imply that an individual caused an aggregate change without evidence and appropriate authority.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Percentage points and relative change are different
sections.explanation: In the lesson’s hypothetical example, a rate rises from 2% to 4%. The difference is two percentage points; the relative increase is 100%.

items.label: Earlier rate
items.detail: The comparison starts at 2%; its population must be defined.

items.label: Later rate
items.detail: 4% is twice 2%, but the absolute rate gap is two percentage points.

sections.takeaway: Neither description tells you the practical impact without counts, denominators and comparable periods.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: A recommendation needs a review and a stop rule
sections.explanation: A bounded pilot is often more defensible than an immediate broad policy change when evidence is preliminary.

items.label: Compare options
items.detail: Show expected benefit, risk and assumptions.

items.label: Name an owner
items.detail: Assign the authorised decision and delivery roles.

items.label: Define evaluation
items.detail: Set timeframe, success and balancing measures.

items.label: State a review trigger
items.detail: Identify evidence that would stop or revise the action.

sections.takeaway: Pair a speed or cost measure with a balancing measure such as quality, access or candidate experience.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: If a rate moves from 2% to 4%, is that a two-percent relative increase?
checkpoint.answer: No. It is a two-percentage-point increase and a 100% relative increase. Show counts and context before interpreting practical importance.

m6-pb4.introduction: A second way to understand “Project Block 4 — Privacy-safe HR dashboard”: read the original explanation, follow the diagram and play or step through its focus points. All practice stays separate from your reading and quiz requirements.

sections.title: Privacy-safe HR dashboard: connect the question to evidence
sections.explanation: An accessible aggregate dashboard and memo whose filters, definitions and disclosure controls have been tested.

items.label: Question
items.detail: An accessible aggregate dashboard and memo whose filters, definitions and disclosure controls have been tested.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Use the original practice material with explicit provenance.

items.label: Decision
items.detail: Explain a bounded recommendation and the evidence that could change it.

sections.takeaway: The app records reading and quizzes; external project submission, verification and marking remain with the institution.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Keep synthetic fixtures and authority boundaries separate
sections.explanation: The practice tables are independent examples, not linked real employee records. Use the original inputs and log every deliberate scenario change.

items.label: Provenance
items.detail: Identify the fixture, grain, period and original source copy.

items.label: Separation
items.detail: Do not join independent populations as if they were one company dataset.

items.label: Permission
items.detail: Use synthetic inputs and the institution-approved submission route.

items.label: Honest context
items.detail: Do not report simulated interviews, approvals or outcomes as live events.

sections.takeaway: No real personal dataset, paid tool or live organisational access is required or authorised by this project.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Reserve time for correction, not only construction
sections.explanation: The original work-plan table supplies the timing. This map groups the work into a review loop without changing those allocations.

items.label: Frame
items.detail: Read the decision and inspect source boundaries.

items.label: Build
items.detail: Create the required artefacts with traceable formulas or decisions.

items.label: Check
items.detail: Reproduce the headline and inspect assumptions and safeguards.

items.label: Review and revise
items.detail: Use peer or self-review and keep a change log.

items.label: Explain and submit
items.detail: Finish the recommendation, disclosure and evidence index.

sections.takeaway: A first draft is not a finished artefact; retain the comment and your response after review.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Organise the privacy-safe hr dashboard submission
sections.explanation: These groups help you locate evidence; the full numbered submission checklist above still defines every required component.

items.label: Wireframe
items.detail: Map each measure to an audience question and action owner.

items.label: Working dashboard
items.detail: Keep period, denominator, refresh, definitions and labels visible.

items.label: Filter QA
items.detail: Test all-data, one-group, empty and combined selections.

items.label: Safe export
items.detail: Review small cells, indirect inference and actual recipient access.

items.label: Insight memo
items.detail: Separate observation, hypotheses, action and evaluation.

sections.takeaway: A public portfolio copy must be safe and clearly labelled; it is not a substitute for the editable institutional submission.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Test whether filters preserve the denominator
sections.explanation: The same synthetic offer cohort supports an all-data view and two source-filtered views. Both sides of each fraction must follow the same selection.

items.label: All data · 75%
items.detail: Nine acceptances ÷ twelve offers.

items.label: Source A · about 83.3%
items.detail: Five acceptances ÷ six Source A offers, not all twelve.

items.label: Source B · about 66.7%
items.detail: Four acceptances ÷ six Source B offers, not all twelve.

sections.takeaway: A filtered numerator must not keep the unfiltered denominator. Also test empty and combined filters and review disclosure before sharing.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Follow the original rubric and its evidence standard
sections.explanation: The original block or capstone marks, performance anchors and institutional award conditions are unchanged.

items.label: Correctness and reproducibility
items.detail: Trace the method and results to the declared source and definitions.

items.label: Judgement and safeguards
items.detail: Show uncertainty, appropriate authority and safe handling.

items.label: Clarity, evidence and reflection
items.detail: Make claims inspectable and explain corrections.

sections.takeaway: These panels and animations do not calculate marks, approve projects or award an external credential.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Review the recommendation from a challenger’s view
sections.explanation: A reviewer should be able to trace a claim, test an assumption and understand which action needs another role’s approval.

items.label: Trace a headline
items.detail: Find the calculation or artefact behind the main claim.

items.label: Challenge an assumption
items.detail: Ask what missing evidence could reverse the action.

items.label: Check authority
items.detail: Name who is permitted to approve a consequential decision.

items.label: Inspect sharing
items.detail: Choose evidence that can safely appear in the public version.

sections.takeaway: Keep the actual review comment and your correction or explanation instead of claiming a review that never happened.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: Explain assistance without outsourcing judgement
sections.explanation: Complete the original AI-use statement even when no AI was used. Tool help must not fabricate records, sources or experience.

items.label: Name tools or none
items.detail: State the actual assistance and permitted synthetic inputs.

items.label: Record your checks
items.detail: Explain accepted, changed and rejected suggestions and independent verification.

items.label: Own the work
items.detail: Describe your contribution, judgement and responsibility for the final claims.

sections.takeaway: Do not upload real employee, candidate, student or credential data to public AI tools; follow exam restrictions separately.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

sections.title: An extension tests an assumption after the core is complete
sections.explanation: The optional extension is not required for full marks. Keep the original work and distinguish a changed scenario from an observation.

items.label: Complete the core
items.detail: Finish the required evidence and safeguards first.

items.label: A deliberately failing filter
items.detail: Demonstrate detection and correction without silently changing the metric definition.

items.label: Compare and document
items.detail: Show what changed, which conclusion depends on it and what remains unknown.

sections.takeaway: More complexity does not improve a submission if the reasoning and safeguards cannot be reproduced.
sections.caption: Illustrative teaching model, not live results, a tool screenshot or an additional assessment requirement.

checkpoint.question: For Source B, should four acceptances be divided by all twelve offers?
checkpoint.answer: No. Use Source B’s six offers: 4/6 is about 66.7%. Filtering only the numerator produces a different, misleading rate; retain the exact counts and definition in the dashboard QA sheet.
